To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
blood pressure is elevated in children receiving solid organs transplants and the blood pressure profile is similar to children with chronic kidney disease.
hypertension, especially nocturnal hypertension, occurs frequently after solid organ transplantation in children and is associated with a high risk of developing cardiovascular disease.

1) hypertension, including nocturnal and daytime hypertension, is present 5 to 8 years after pediatric solid organ transplantation; 2) ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM), including nocturnal blood pressure dipping, is an important tool in the follow‐ up of pediatric transplant recipients; 3) the ABPM profile is not affected by antihypertensive treatment; and 4) ABPM parameters do not correlate well with metabolic parameters, kidney function, or graft function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the blood pressure profiles in children after transplantation.
the long‐term effects of solid organ transplantation in children and young adults.
hypertension in pediatric solid organ recipients and its association to cardiovascular risk and metabolic disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ABPM is a valuable diagnostic and monitoring tool in pediatric patients receiving solid organ transplant.
the use of ABPM is important in the follow‐ups of children with solid organ transplants.
the use of ABPM is recommended in children with solid organ transplant, as it is a valuable tool in the assessment of hypertension, especially in the presence of nocturnal hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ABPM profiles of pediatric solid organ recipients are similar and characterized by abnormal BP load and nocturnal BP dipping.
the use of 24‐hour ABPM in the pediatric transplant population can be helpful to detect hypertension and to identify patients who need more aggressive treatment.
the use of ABPM should be recommended in the follow up of children after solid organ transplantation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ABPM profiles of children with solid organ transplant are similar, with a high proportion of abnormal nocturnal BP profiles.
ABPM is an essential tool to monitor the BP status in the follow‐ups of pediatric solid organ transplant recipients.
ABPM is a valuable tool for the diagnosis and follow‐up of pediatric transplant patients.
